prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Conservative Party Manifesto 2024 – Summary (under 500 words)

Core theme: “A secure future” by sticking to a long-term plan: lower taxes, controlled migration, stronger defence, better public services, pragmatic net zero, stronger families and communities.

Economy and tax
- Cut employee National Insurance to 6% by April 2027; abolish main rate NI for the self‑employed by end of Parliament; no rises to income tax or VAT.
- Triple Lock Plus: uprate State Pension and create an age‑related personal allowance so the State Pension stays tax‑free; no new pension taxes.
- Support pay: maintain National Living Wage at two‑thirds of median earnings (c.£13 by 2029).
- Business: keep corporation tax; expand full expensing (including leasing when affordable); 10‑point SME plan (rates relief, finance, prompt payment, fewer reporting burdens).
- Infrastructure/innovation: £36bn HS2 savings into local transport; gigabit to nationwide by 2030; 5G/6G ambition; public R&D to £22bn; £1.5bn+ for AI compute; £4.5bn advanced manufacturing plan.
- Trade/regulation: build on CPTPP; seek India/GCC FTAs; maintain sovereignty in EU TCA review; use Brexit freedoms to cut red tape; civil service back to pre‑Covid size; 2% annual public‑sector productivity target.

Families, childcare and education
- 30 free childcare hours from nine months to school (by Sept 2025); move Child Benefit to household test with taper £120k–£160k.
- Mandatory National Service at 18 (paid competitive military year or civic service, 25 days).
- 100,000 extra apprenticeships funded by closing poor‑outcome degrees; Advanced British Standard for 16–19; statutory ban on phones in school; expand PE and school competitions.
- SEND: 60,000 more places; 15 new special free schools.

Borders, asylum and legal migration
- Monthly removals to Rwanda; clear asylum claims in six months; crack down on smuggling; seek international asylum reforms.
- Legal, binding annual migration cap on work/family visas that falls each year; higher salary thresholds; pre‑travel health checks; higher IHS/fees; restrict dependants.

Defence, security and veterans
- Defence spending to 2.5% of GDP by 2030; £10bn munitions; MoD R&D at 5% plus 2% exploitation; back Ukraine; modernise procurement.
- Veterans Bill; NI holiday for veteran employers; extend visa fee waivers to dependants.

NHS, dentistry and social care
- NHS funding up above inflation yearly; +92k nurses and +28k doctors; Pharmacy First; 250 GP surgeries; 50 more Community Diagnostic Centres.
- £3.4bn tech upgrade (NHS App “single front door”, AI diagnostics, data platform); cut 5,500 managers.
- Dental Recovery Plan (+2.5m appointments; NHS service requirement for new dentists; rural “golden hellos”).
- Social care: cap from Oct 2025; multi‑year council settlements; support unpaid carers.
- Mental health: teams in all schools and colleges by 2030; early support hubs; bigger Talking Therapies; new mental health law.
- Implement Cass Review; protect single‑sex wards and language.

Welfare and work
- Reform PIP and Work Capability Assessment; move fit notes to specialists; tougher sanctions after 12 months; Universal Credit rollout; Fraud Bill; target £12bn/yr savings.

Housing, transport and communities
- 1.6m homes; fast‑track brownfield in 20 biggest cities; raise London densities; new Help to Buy; permanent FTB Stamp Duty relief to £425k; leasehold reform; renters reform with court changes to end Section 21.
- 8,000 more neighbourhood police; hotspot policing; tougher sentences for serious crime and VAWG; anti‑fraud measures.
- Back drivers: ban road pricing; reverse London ULEZ expansion; local referendums for LTNs/20mph; extend £2 bus fare cap for the Parliament; Rail Reform Bill creating Great British Railways.

Energy, net zero and environment
- Pragmatic net zero by 2050; no new green levies; maintain price cap; review standing charges; energy‑efficiency vouchers and £6bn upgrades; annual North Sea licensing; new gas plants; treble offshore wind; scale nuclear (SMRs, Wylfa); CCS clusters; import carbon pricing by 2027; protect best farmland from solar; retain fracking moratorium.
- Farming: budget +£1bn over Parliament, legal food security target, fast‑track farm infrastructure, tapered seasonal worker route; replicate £100m Seafood Fund.
- Environment: record flood funding; Plan for Water with tougher sanctions; more tree planting; new National Park; expand access to nature.

Union and devolved nations
- Protect internal market; extend UK Shared Prosperity Fund; more Freeports/Investment Zones; targeted transport/industry pledges in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland; oppose Scottish independence; support Windsor Framework.
